purpose: Targeted additions to data/train for candidate-r2, aimed at the act / don't-act boundary. Priority: false-positive executable actions, no-tool misclassification, high-severity false actions, missing-slot execution, stale-context misuse, cancel/correction, wrong-tool, then argument normalization. Positive actions are added alongside so tool recall does not collapse under a much larger no-action set.

derivedFrom.observation: local base and candidate-r1 show the same 13 failure families at the same counts on the LF corpus: 10 false-positive executable actions (3 high_impact), 14 false-positive tool calls, 3 missing-slot executions, 4 stale-context misuses, 1 cancel-produced action, 1 wrong tool, 3 unit-normalization errors.

_rule: Every example is authored for training only. None reuses an eval id or an eval utterance (checked by `python -m vesta_router validate` on normalized utterances), and a stricter token-overlap screen (Jaccard >= 0.5 against every eval utterance) was run before writing: nine candidates that were near-copies of specific eval cases were reworded or dropped. The three remaining pairs at 0.6 share only a generic command frame and have different expected outcomes.
_familyNote: addedByFamily counts overlap (an acknowledgement answers both false-positive families and the lexical-grounding one). addedByPrimaryFamily counts each example once, by its first target. `tool-recall-guard` is not a failure family: it marks positive actions added so recall does not collapse. The per-example list is authoritative.
